previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Meléndez, a man with a history of dilated cardiomyopathy, systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and chronic alcohol use, was admitted for hematemesis and abdominal pain. He reported vomiting several cups of blood and had a history of gastritis. Initial concerns for mesenteric ischemia due to rising lactate were ruled out by abdominal CTA, which showed patent vasculature. He was treated with IV pantoprazole, fluids, and symptom management. His condition stabilized, with no further bleeding, and he tolerated a gradual diet advancement. His heart medications, including metoprolol, losartan, and Pradaxa, were restarted. He expressed interest in alcohol rehabilitation, and plans were made for transfer to a facility post-discharge. He was discharged home with follow-up instructions and prescriptions.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old gentleman with history of HTN, afib, dilated 
cardiomyopathy, systolic CHF (EF 25% in ___, STEMI ___ 
s/p cardiac catherization, VT s/p AICD, PE in ___ s/p 6 
months of enoxaparin, p/w report of assault to chest ___, 
transferred to MICU for alcohol withdrawal and persistent 
lactate elevation to 3 without evidence or source of sepsis. He 
was transferred to floor for management of ongoing CP, Etoh 
withdrawal, hematemesis, and workup of syncope.

# Alcohol abuse and withdrawal: He has a long hx of abuse with 
history of DTs and seizures in the past.  He was initially 
admitted to the MICU due to large need for benzo administration 
and consistently had CIWA scores in the ___.  He had a 
significant amount of vomiting felt to be due to withdrawal.  
Valium was tapered and he eventually no longer required any.  He 
was seen by SW and discharge to ___ house was 
pursued but there were no beds available.  He was counseled to 
abstain from alcohol use.

# Hematemesis:  On transfer to the floor from the MICU, he 
endorsed coffee ground emesis with small amts of blood.  This 
was felt to ___ tear vs gastritis.  Past EGD in 
___ showed gastritis without varices.  He was placed on IV 
protonix and remained hemodynamically stable with stable Hct.  
He continued to complain of mild amounts of vomiting blood, but 
refused to save his vomitus for nursing/MDs to see.  He did have 
multiple episodes of vomiting of completely undigested food that 
he saved and was noted to not have blood present.  His PPI was 
changed to oral.  On discharge he was given a prescription for a 
PPI but refused to take it with him.  He also complained of 
blowing his nose and seeing blood and then coughing up a small 
amount of blood and he may have had a small nosebleed.

# Chest pain: He complained of chest pain on admission at the 
site of his ICD.  He had recently been assaulted and stated that 
he was punched in that area.  this pain improved with oxycodone. 
 He also complained of chest pain during admission which he 
described as a stabbing pain that awoke him from sleep.  He had 
serial ECGs and was noted to have new TWI in the lateral 
precordial leads (V5-V6), although his ECG changes did not 
correlate with onset of his stabbing chest pain.  Upon review of 
many old ECGs in our system, it appeared that he has had similar 
ECG changes in the past as well.  He was ruled out for MI and 
continued on telemetry.  His chest pain did not improve with 
nitro but improved with oxycodone.  He had inconsistent reports 
of the quality and duration of his symptoms.  At the time of 
discharge, he was pacing the halls most of the day without any 
exertional symptoms.

# Dizziness/Syncope: He reported episodes of syncope and 
receiving shocks x 4 in the past month prior to admission.  He 
had no further episodes here and was monitored on telemetry 
without any abnormality.  His ICD was interrogated and showed no 
abnormality and no shocks had been delivered.

# Chronic systolic CHF EF25% with dilated CMP: He is nonadherent 
to his medications and actively using alcohol.  He remained 
euvolemic on this admission and was continued on his home 
prescribed medications.

# HTN: Continued on home beta blocker and ___.

# Facial pain: Had tenderness and bruising of his face with low 
likelihood of fracture, felt to be related to recent assault.

# Afib: His pradaxa was initially held due to concern for 
hematemesis but then restarted prior to discharge.

# Cough: He complained of cough during admission and had a CXR 
which was clear.  Felt to be possible bronchitis.
